content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Attendance shows a clear wave of illness. Payments has 15 absences against a usual 2.8; 12 agents went home unwell after lunch and 3 called in sick. General has 13 absences against a usual 2.6; 10 went home unwell and 3 called in sick. As a result, staffing is 18% short on payments and 16% short on general. Agents on phones have been running about 4–5 below plan every interval since 18:15. Demand is not the driver. Payments volume is roughly on forecast over the last hour, and general is below forecast, with no reason spiking abnormally. The marketing calendar is empty, and the only incident is a branch-only printer issue. Service level has slipped to 78.9% on payments and 73.3% on general in the latest interval.","plan_name":"Final 45 minutes: protect capacity on both queues with low-cost levers","rationale":"Only 45 minutes remain. New overtime would arrive 30 minutes after approval and cover just 19:45–20:00. Roughly Rs 11,500 of the Rs 15,000 budget is already committed to accepted overtime, so further overtime is poor value. Moving agents between queues won't help because both queues are short and below or near 70–80% service level. The plan therefore uses free or cheap levers that act immediately: (1) Delay breaks from 19:15 to 20:00 on both queues. This keeps agents on phones through close. General agents already delayed at 13:45 are skipped automatically, so this mainly helps payments, which has had no delay yet. (2) Cancel any non-mandatory coaching left before close; the earlier cancellation only ran to 17:00. (3) Deflect up to 20% of simple status and balance enquiries to chat at Rs 12 per chat. These are payment_status_enquiry and refund_status on payments, and balance_enquiry on general. (4) Offer callbacks on general, the weaker queue, to cap long waits and abandonment; accepted callbacks can be worked after the peak.
